name: Beetles and Other Friends
description:
In the insect world you will find:

Cicadas that carry their own drums within their bodies

Ants that keep pet blights in their nests, so they can suck out their sweet juices, much as we milk cows and goats

Spiders that use web strings to swing from—just like a favourite action hero

And many more fascinating and bizarre facts about these tiny beings that live among us.

name: The Red Wind Howls
description:
‘Part Gulag Archipelago, part One Hundred Years of Solitude, The Red Wind Howls…[is an] urgent, tragic, and vital testimony for the Tibetan people.’—Woeser, author of Forbidden Memory: Tibet During the Cultural Revolution

‘This is Tsering D?ndrup’s boldest and most meticulously researched novel yet. Capturing the complex and tragic existence of Tibet under Chinese occupation, the book is as much about human suffering as it is about moral courage and the survival of a civilization.’

name: The World Was Not Their Story
description: With few correspondents overseas, independent India’s newspapers have depended on agencies and publications in London or Washington, content to wear the blinkers of the West. The world, in other words, was not their story. Saeed Naqvi spent his sixty-year career trying to make it one. His journey began at The Statesman in the 1960s, where he made his name with an exclusive on the Beatles in Rishikesh and won Jayaprakash Narayan’s confidence while reporting the Bihar movement.
